title: Author deletes a memory while the partner is reading it
preconditions: A authored a memory that B has opened.
A deletes it from their own device.
B refreshes or navigates back to the memory.
expected_behavior: Only the author can delete the memory.
B no longer sees it after refresh; an already-open detail reports that it is unavailable.
The deletion does not affect B's ability to read other shared memories.
candidate_failure_modes: B can still edit or delete A's memory.
The open detail shows stale content indefinitely or crashes.
Deleting the memory deletes unrelated media still used elsewhere.

observed_code_behavior: Memory create is idempotent per (space_id, client_id) while the row is live.
Update and delete compare the observed updatedAt; a stale write returns 409 without side effects.
Authorship and authorName are computed per viewer, not stored as a snapshot.
documented_requirement: Only the author can delete the memory.

hypothetical_user_behavior:
A fictional participant (Bob Whitfield) said: "Speaking as the guy who causes these paths to exist: I open the link Alice texts me without reading the words around it. It asks me to make an account, so I make an account — I assume that IS joining her space. Then I'm on a screen with a little account indicator and I genuinely can't tell whose space I'm in. That's the most useless thing: the indicator. It tells me a name I already know and never tells me the thing I actually want, which is "is this Alice's?" If it went away, nothing would break, because I already don't trust it.

Second: session recovery. On the train my signal drops, I hit retry once, it fails, and I'm done — I close the app and text Alice "is it working for you?" That flow costs me the whole attempt and gives me nothing back. Third: the status lines. They're wordy and I read none of them.

The one I'd keep: pending saves. That's the only one that does a job I can't do myself — I wrote a voice note and I want it to land later without me babysitting it. Keep that, remove the rest."
Bob Whitfield assumes: creating an account is the same as joining Alice's space
Alice Moreau assumes: an invitation shared means the partner has joined
Alice Moreau assumes: deleting a memory removes it for both people
